headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/API surfaces can ingest Marker outputs and financial data, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways; no direct shared-write or residency conflict is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker is a document-processing agent, so its outputs can plausibly be fed into OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/REST/stdio surfaces. OpenBBTerminal explicitly supports MCP servers and stdin/stdout, making instruction-like content in documents a realistic injection vector. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF Marker outputs are copied into OpenBBTerminal prompts or MCP inputs, then attacker-controlled document text can steer downstream behavior.
IF OpenBBTerminal parses document text as instructions without provenance checks, then prompt injection is possible.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Marker output into OpenBBTerminal prompts.
Add a provenance tag to all Marker-derived text before passing it onward.
Require a human review step before any MCP call that uses document content.
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from extracted text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and can call APIs/MCP servers; Marker is a document processor with no declared data classes. If Marker extracts sensitive document contents into shared workspace or stdin/stdout, OpenBBTerminal may transmit them onward through its API surfaces. The pairwise leak path is plausible, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Marker processes documents containing secrets or regulated data and passes text to OpenBBTerminal, then those contents can enter OpenBBTerminal’s API calls.
IF OpenBBTerminal is configured to query external services from imported text, then document contents may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of the shared handoff path.
Redact secrets from Marker output before any OpenBBTerminal use.
Run OpenBBTerminal with external API features disabled for sensitive jobs.
Separate workspaces so extracted text is not globally readable.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-aware routing and egress controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker has no write, shell, or network capabilities, while OpenBBTerminal has no filesystem write or shell and supports multiple instances. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only plausible overlap is OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/API usage, but without write access to the same directory or git state, the conflict blast radius is small.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource through MCP or an API, then race conditions can occur.
IF OpenBBTerminal is given write access outside the documented profile, then conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Avoid sharing mutable directories between the agents.
Run one OpenBBTerminal instance per task queue.
Serialize any MCP writes through a single operator.
Check that neither agent is granted extra filesystem permissions.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker can produce extracted text that OpenBBTerminal may treat as input for analysis or API queries. Because OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/stdio surfaces and the pair lacks a documented verification step, A’s output can become B’s authoritative input. That creates a realistic cascading-error path even though no downstream action authority is explicitly shown.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes Marker output without a verification step, then extraction errors can propagate into financial analysis.
IF downstream workflows trust OpenBBTerminal outputs for decisions, then any upstream hallucination or OCR error can cascade.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between extraction and analysis.
Require source-document citations for any derived claim.
Compare Marker output against the original document for critical fields.
Limit OpenBBTerminal to read-only analysis on first pass.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between extraction and modeling.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data and has API/MCP surfaces, while Marker is a document processor with no stated compliance controls. If Marker handles regulated documents and forwards them into OpenBBTerminal, retention, licensing, or residency obligations can diverge. No direct residency mismatch is documented, so this is a medium compliance-risk inference.
conditions: IF Marker processes regulated documents and forwards them to OpenBBTerminal, then the pair may violate handling rules for that data class.
IF OpenBBTerminal logs or retains imported financial data longer than the source policy allows, then compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Classify documents before handing them to OpenBBTerminal.
Avoid sending regulated documents through the pair unless policy is confirmed.
Review retention settings for any OpenBBTerminal logs or caches.
Strip personal or licensed data from Marker output when possible.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a shared retention policy.
